summary:
AgriCloud is a planting-advice prototype for farmers and extension workers in Uganda. Our first test site is Soroti district.

Farmers plant on fixed dates (15 March and 15 August). But the rains start on a different day each year.

We used 35 years of NASA POWER daily rainfall (1991-2025). We checked it against CHIRPS rainfall. We found the start of the rains for each year. Then we compared it with the fixed dates.

On NASA POWER, 15 March came before the rains in 25 of 35 years. The two rainfall records do not agree on how often. We show both results.

The farmer gives past crops. Soil pH and planting date are optional. The app tells the farmer what to plant, when, and why. The advice comes from the rain analysis and a crop-rules table with sources.

One fixed date cannot fit every year. AgriCloud helps farmers plant when the rains start.
details:
AgriCloud helps a farmer decide what to plant and when to plant it.

The farmer or extension worker enters the crops from past seasons. AgriCloud finds the district from the location. Soil pH and moisture are optional.

The tool compares the rain start date in each past year with the fixed planting dates.

We used two rainfall sources, NASA POWER and CHIRPS, and we show both.

The tool then scores each crop path, for example maize then beans, with crop rules from the MAAIF manual.

Where we did not find a source, the rule is marked as an assumption.

The result is a short card with the best planting window, other crop options and the reasons.

The result can be translated into local languages. We start with Ateso.

The method works for any district. We tested it first in Soroti with maize, beans and millet.
